attempted_reduction: scipy (13.9 MB) and scikit-learn (4.4 MB) arrive as LightGBM dependencies this page never imports; micropip.install("lightgbm", deps=False) does not avoid them, because micropip defers to Pyodide's own dependency graph for distributed packages. Tried and measured.

compression.at_rest: Boosters: 30,823,690 B of model text -> 11,125,154 B gzip -> 14,833,552 B base64, decoded in the browser. Base64 costs 3.7 MB over binary gzip on a first visit and keeps the model off the uncacheable redirect path. Lossless; the equivalence gate proves the decoded model bitwise.
compression.not_compressed: marimo's interface assets are served as marimo emits them.
compression.platform: none — Hugging Face Static Spaces serve files as stored

contrast_with_the_static_page: docs/index.html fetches nothing: 1 request (itself), 0 resources, verified in a browser. At CP-3, marimo export html was rejected for it because it emitted 181 references to cdn.jsdelivr.net. marimo export html-wasm differs in kind: it bundles marimo's frontend with the page and reaches a CDN only for the Python runtime.

us.aws.cdn.hf.co.source: DevTools, first visit (served by the emulator)

yarden-viktor-delu-day-ahead-forecast.st.source: DevTools, first visit (served by the emulator)

method: headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol, brand-new profile, page and every worker attached. Bytes are DevTools encodedDataLength: what Chrome received per request, headers and body, as encoded. DevTools is not subject to Timing-Allow-Origin, so every host is sized directly. Reproduce: make wasm && uv run python scripts/record_wasm_load.py (writes reports/cp3b/cdp_load.json).

platform_serving_model.binary_files: 302 from the static host with Cache-Control: no-store and a 1,048-byte body, to us.aws.cdn.hf.co with a signed query that changed on each of three consecutive requests; both hops send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.
platform_serving_model.consequence_for_design: The nine boosters ship as base64-encoded gzip — ASCII text, served directly — rather than binary gzip, which would be routed through the rotating signed redirect on every visit. marimo's fonts and images are binary and unavoidably take the redirect.
platform_serving_model.text_files: 200 from the Space's static host, no Content-Encoding even to a client sending gzip, deflate, br; ETag present; no Cache-Control.
platform_serving_model.verified_on: live public Static Spaces (nanotron/ultrascale-playbook, xenova/whisper-web), read-only, 2026-09-15

repeat_visit.what: Same profile, second visit: the page's text revalidated (304s), jsDelivr, PyPI and the marimo lockfile came from cache, and the fonts and images behind the no-store redirects were fetched again (970,079 B).

revision: Final: measured in headless Chrome 152 over the DevTools protocol with a brand-new profile, page and Pyodide worker attached, against emulated Hugging Face serving (HTTP/1.1; text direct with ETag; binary files as a no-store 302 to a CDN stand-in). Supersedes the earlier stitched measurements, which missed browser favicon/manifest requests and used an HTTP/1.0 emulator.
self_reference: The Space serves files that print this size, so an exact byte count drifts by a few bytes whenever the wording changes; the surfaces publish two-decimal millions, which that drift cannot move.

totals.plain_language: about 57 MB on a first visit (57,252,166 bytes), 352 requests from 5 hosts

units_note: Published in decimal megabytes (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes) to two decimals, with exact bytes here.

via_the_huggingface_page.what: Opening the canonical Space link loads Hugging Face's own page, which runs the app in an iframe from the static host. Measured once, read-only, on 2026-09-15 against the already-created Space (then holding template files): the wrapper's document (12,685 B) plus 201 resource entries — huggingface.co 190 requests 953,085 B, js.stripe.com 2 requests 247,693 B, cdnjs.cloudflare.com 1 request 2,955 B, de5282c3ca0c.edge.sdk.awswaf.com 6 requests (sizes not disclosed by the browser), and the static host 2 requests (the iframe, sized inside it). Hugging Face controls that page and it may change; the app's own figures do not include it.
